titulo: Media / News, lifestyles and current affairs
descripcion_es: The press, radio, television, social media and the news.
resumen: Vocabulary to talk about how you keep informed, discuss the news and talk about the press, television and social media.

explicacion.texto: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb even though it ends in -s: The news is on at nine; a piece of news (es: una noticia). The media can take a singular or a plural verb. Watch out for false friends: a newspaper article is not a “periódico artículo”, and an editorial is not “una editorial” (which is a publisher).

filas: newspapers, TV, radio, etc. as a whole (es: los medios de comunicación)
The press was not allowed in.
daily paper / weekly or monthly publication (es: periódico / revista)
I read a newspaper on the train.
the title of a news story (es: titular)
a piece of writing / an account of an event (es: artículo / reportaje, crónica)
There's an interesting report on housing.
the first page of a newspaper (es: portada)
It was on the front page.
a person who writes or reports news (es: periodista / reportero)
the person in charge of a newspaper or its content (es: director, redactor jefe)
The editor decided to publish it.
a company that publishes books (es: editorial)
The publisher released the book in May.
send out on radio or TV (es: emitir, retransmitir)
The match will be broadcast live.
shown as it happens (es: en directo)
The debate is live on Channel 4.
a person who introduces a programme (es: presentador)
reports of recent events / the news programme (es: las noticias, el telediario)
news reported as it happens (es: noticia de última hora)
Breaking news: the airport is closed.
websites and apps for sharing content (es: redes sociales)
I spend too much time on social media.
put online / pass on to others (es: publicar / compartir)
She posted a photo and many people shared it.
a person who follows an account (es: seguidor)
spread very fast on the internet (es: hacerse viral)
false stories presented as news (es: noticias falsas, bulos)
favouring one side / fair and neutral (es: parcial, sesgado / imparcial)
the reporting of an event (es: cobertura informativa)
The coverage of the election was excellent.
pay to receive something regularly (es: suscribirse a)
I subscribe to a digital newspaper.
I listen to podcasts on my way to work.

items: “Una noticia” is a piece of news or a news story, never “a new”.
Advertisement / advert / ad = a notice promoting a product (es: anuncio); advertise = promote publicly (es: anunciar).
With networks and broadcasting, on: on social media, on Twitter, on the radio, on TV, but in the newspaper.

ejemplos.frase: I heard an interesting piece of news on the radio this morning.
ejemplos.traduccion: Esta mañana oí una noticia interesante en la radio.

ejemplos.frase: The scandal was on the front page of every newspaper.
ejemplos.traduccion: El escándalo salió en la portada de todos los periódicos.

ejemplos.frase: The final will be broadcast live in more than 100 countries.
ejemplos.traduccion: La final se retransmitirá en directo en más de cien países.

ejemplos.frase: Her post about the lost dog went viral.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su publicación sobre el perro perdido se hizo viral.

ejemplos.frase: Many people get their news from social media rather than newspapers.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mucha gente se informa por las redes sociales en lugar de por los periódicos.

ejemplos.frase: The coverage of the floods was criticised as biased.
ejemplos.traduccion: La cobertura de las inundaciones fue criticada por sesgada.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I have a good new for you.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have some good news for you.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: News is uncountable; “a new” does not exist.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The news are very bad today.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The news is very bad today.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: My novel was published by a big editorial.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: My novel was published by a big publisher.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: “Editorial” (the company) is publisher; an editorial is an opinion article in a newspaper.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I read it on the newspaper.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I read it in the newspaper.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In the newspaper, but on TV / on the radio / on the internet.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of be.
ejercicios.frase: The news ___ (be) on at nine o'clock every night.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that news is uncountable and takes a singular verb even though it ends in -s: “The news is on at nine”. The clue is the subject The news: the -s does not indicate a plural, so the verb be is in the third person singular, is. The contraction 's is also accepted. “Be on” here means “be broadcast, be shown on TV”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las noticias (el telediario) empiezan a las nueve todas las noches.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “las noticias son”: news is uncountable and always takes a singular verb.
The verb must be conjugated: with a third person singular subject it is is.
It is singular, but every night indicates a present habit; the right tense is the present, is.

glosario.definicion_l: appear in a show, on T.V. or radio

ejercicios.frase: I saw the interview ___ TV last night.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that we say on TV, on the radio and on social media, but in the newspaper. The clue is TV: with media that are broadcast or viewed on a screen or a device we use on. The result is “I saw the interview on TV”. Spanish “en la tele” leads learners to copy in, which is not correct here.
ejercicios.traduccion: Anoche vi la entrevista en la tele.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of “en la tele”: with TV we use on; in is for in the newspaper.
At is not used with the media; the preposition is on.
By would indicate the means by which something is sent (by post), not where a programme is seen.

glosario.definicion_l: the questioning of a person (or a conversation in which information is elicited); often conducted by journalists · a conference (usually with someone important)

ejercicios.frase: The ___ on the front page said «Prices up again».
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “headline” (es: “titular”), next to “front page” (es: “portada”). The clue is the quotation and the reference to the front page: what appears highlighted at the top is the headline. Headline is formed from head and line. The result is “The headline on the front page said…”.
ejercicios.traduccion: El titular de la portada decía «Los precios vuelven a subir».

errores_previstos.explicacion: Title is the title of a book or a film; the title of a news story is the headline.
Holder is “titular” in the sense of owner (of an account, a post); it is not a newspaper headline.
Heading is a section heading in a text; in the press we say headline.

glosario.definicion_l: the heading or caption of a newspaper article · publicize widely or highly, as if with a headline

ejercicios.frase: The video of the singing cat went ___ in a few hours.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “go viral” (es: “hacerse viral”). The clue is the verb went, past of go, which in this collocation means “become”. The result is “went viral in a few hours”. In English we do not say “make viral” or “become virus”: go viral is the fixed expression for content that spreads very quickly on the internet.
ejercicios.traduccion: El vídeo del gato que canta se hizo viral en pocas horas.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Virus is the noun; after go we need the adjective viral.
It is an adverb; the fixed expression uses the adjective: go viral.
Go famous does not exist (you would say become famous) and it does not have the meaning of mass spreading on the internet.

ejercicios.frase: That's a very interesting ___ of news.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that “una noticia” is a piece of news or a news story, never “a new”. The clue is “of news” after the gap: news is uncountable, so to count one unit we use the partitive structure a piece of. The result is “a very interesting piece of news”. Notice is a false friend.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “Una noticia” is a piece of news.

por_opcion.piece: Correct. A piece of news is the way to count one item of news, because news is uncountable.
por_opcion.new: Incorrect. New is the adjective (es: “nuevo”); “a new of news” makes no sense and “a new” does not mean “una noticia”.
por_opcion.notice: Incorrect. Notice is a false friend: it means a sign or announcement, or advance warning (es: “aviso, anuncio”, “preaviso”), not “noticia”.

glosario.definicion_l: an announcement containing information about an event · the act of noticing or paying attention

ejercicios.frase: This channel only gives one side of the story. It's very ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “biased / unbiased” (es: “parcial, sesgado / imparcial”). The clue is the first sentence: if a channel only tells one side of the story, it is biased. The result is “It's very biased”. Live and viral have nothing to do with impartiality.
ejercicios.traduccion: Este canal solo da una versión de la historia. Es muy parcial.

por_opcion.biased: Correct. Biased means favouring one side (es: “parcial, sesgado”), exactly what we say of a channel that only gives one version.
por_opcion.live: Incorrect. Live means shown as it happens (es: “en directo”); it describes how something is broadcast, not whether the information is impartial.
por_opcion.viral: Incorrect. Viral is said of content that is widely shared on the internet, not of a biased channel.

glosario.significado: una sola versión de los hechos

ejercicios.frase: The concert will be ___ live on national radio.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “broadcast” (es: “emitir, retransmitir”), with the example “The match will be broadcast live”. The clue is “live on national radio”: radio and television broadcast; they do not publish or print. Broadcast is irregular and its past participle is the same as the infinitive, which is why “will be broadcast” has no -ed.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To send out on radio or television is broadcast.
ejercicios.traduccion: El concierto se retransmitirá en directo por la radio nacional.

por_opcion.broadcast: Correct. Broadcast means to send out on radio or television (es: “emitir, retransmitir”); the past participle is the same as the infinitive.
por_opcion.published: Incorrect. Publish is used for books, newspapers or written content, not for radio broadcasts.
por_opcion.printed: Incorrect. Print means to put on paper (es: “imprimir”); it makes no sense with a concert on the radio.

glosario.definicion_l: message that is transmitted by radio or television · a radio or television show
actually being performed at the time of hearing or viewing · exerting force or containing energy

ejercicios.frase: Before you share a story, check the ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “source” (es: “fuente”), with the example “Always check your sources”. The clue is the context of sharing a piece of information: we are talking about its origin. Spanish “fuente” has several meanings that English separates: source is the origin of information, fountain is the water fountain in a square and font is the typeface.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The source of information is source; fountain is a water fountain.
ejercicios.traduccion: Antes de compartir una noticia, comprueba la fuente.

por_opcion.source: Correct. Source is the origin of a piece of information, which you must check before sharing it.
por_opcion.fountain: Incorrect. Fountain is a water fountain, like the one in a square.
por_opcion.font: Incorrect. Font is the typeface on a computer; it is also a false friend of “fuente”.

glosario.definicion_l: the place where something begins, where it springs into being · a document (or organization) from which information is obtained
assets belonging to or due to or contributed by an individual person or group

ejercicios.frase: She works for an editorial that publishes children's books.
respuestas: She works for a publisher that publishes children's books.
She works for a publishing house that publishes children's books.
She works for a publishing company that publishes children's books.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card warns that an editorial is not “una editorial”, which is a publisher; an editorial is an opinion article in a newspaper. The clue is “that publishes children's books”: we are talking about a company that publishes books. The correction is “a publisher”, “a publishing house” or “a publishing company”; notice that the article changes to a because publisher begins with a consonant.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The publishing company is a publisher or publishing house.
ejercicios.traduccion: Trabaja para una editorial que publica libros infantiles.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works for an editorial that publishes children's books.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: an editorial is an opinion article, not a publishing company.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works for an publisher that publishes children's books.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The word is correct, but before publisher the article is a, not an.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She works for an editor that publishes children's books.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Editor is a person (the head of a newspaper or chief editor), not the company; it would also need a, not an.

glosario.definicion_l: of or relating to an article stating opinions or giving perspectives · relating to or characteristic of an editor

ejercicios.frase: I have two good news for you.
respuestas: I have two pieces of good news for you.
I have two bits of good news for you.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card reminds you that news is uncountable: it cannot go directly with a number. The clue is two, which requires counting units; for this we use the partitive pieces of (or, more informally, bits of). The result is “two pieces of good news”. The adjective good goes before news, inside the partitive phrase.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: News is uncountable: two pieces of news.
ejercicios.traduccion: Tengo dos buenas noticias para ti.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have two good news for you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: news is uncountable and cannot take numbers.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have two good new for you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: New is the adjective (es: “nuevo”); “a new” does not exist as “una noticia”.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I have two piece of good news for you.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With two, the countable noun piece goes in the plural: two pieces.

ejercicios.frase: I read the article on yesterday's newspaper.
respuestas: I read the article in yesterday's newspaper.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card points out that we say in the newspaper, but on TV, on the radio and on the internet. The clue is newspaper: the text is inside the pages of the newspaper, which is why we use in. The correction is “in yesterday's newspaper”. The mistake comes from generalising on from audiovisual media.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: In a newspaper is in the newspaper.
ejercicios.traduccion: Leí el artículo en el periódico de ayer.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I read the article on yesterday's newspaper.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: with newspaper the preposition is in.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I read the article at yesterday's newspaper.
errores_previstos.explicacion: At is not used for the place where a text appears; with newspaper it is in.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I read the article in the yesterday's newspaper.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The possessive yesterday's already acts as a determiner; it cannot also take the.

respuestas: She spends too much time on social media
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “social media” (es: “redes sociales”), and the card points out that we say on social media. The sentence follows the structure spend + time + on something: “She spends too much time on social media”. Too much goes before time because time is uncountable. The order is subject, verb, time phrase and the preposition on with the medium.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: “En redes sociales” is on social media.
ejercicios.traduccion: Pasa demasiado tiempo en las redes sociales.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She spends much too time on social media
errores_previstos.explicacion: Too goes before much: too much time.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She spends too much time social on media
errores_previstos.explicacion: Social media is a fixed phrase: the adjective social goes before media, after the preposition on.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Too much time she spends on social media
errores_previstos.explicacion: Putting the complement first is a marked order that does not correspond to a neutral sentence; English puts the subject and verb first.

glosario.definicion_l: Interactive forms of media that allow users to interact with and publish to each other, generally by means of the Internet

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives the example “The story made the headlines”, that is, appear in the headlines, be front-page news (es: “salir en los titulares, ser noticia de portada”). It is a fixed collocation with the verb make in the past and headlines in the plural with the. The order is subject (The story), verb (made) and complement (the headlines). Story here means a news item (es: “noticia”), not a tale (es: “cuento”).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Make the headlines means appear in the headlines.
ejercicios.traduccion: La noticia salió en los titulares.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It swaps the subject and the complement: it is the story that makes the headlines.
The verb goes between the subject and the complement: The story made the headlines.

glosario.definicion_l: a message that tells the particulars of an act or occurrence or course of events; presented in writing or drama or cinema or as a radio or television program · a piece of fiction that narrates a chain of related events

ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “subscribe to” (es: “suscribirse a”). The clue is the verb subscribe, which always takes the preposition to. The result is “I subscribe to two online newspapers”. In English the present simple expresses the habitual situation: there is no need for a structure like Spanish “estoy suscrito”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Estoy suscrito a dos periódicos digitales.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Subscribe is not used with at; the fixed preposition is to.
A calque of “inscribirse en”: subscribe takes to.
That is the Spanish preposition; in English it is subscribe to.

ejercicios.frase: The ___ of the election on public TV was very thorough.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “coverage” (es: “cobertura informativa”). The clue is the article The and the preposition of: we need a noun that refers to the way the media report an event. Coverage is the fixed word for this, formed from cover (“report on a news story”). Covering and cover exist, but they do not have this meaning.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The reporting of an event is coverage.
ejercicios.traduccion: La cobertura de las elecciones en la televisión pública fue muy completa.

por_opcion.coverage: Correct. Coverage is the reporting that a medium gives to an event.
por_opcion.covering: Incorrect. Covering is a layer or case that covers something (a floor covering), not journalistic coverage.
por_opcion.cover: Incorrect. Cover is the front of a magazine or a lid; it does not refer to the reporting of an election.

glosario.definicion_l: the total amount and type of insurance carried · the extent to which something is covered
painstakingly careful and accurate · performed comprehensively and completely; not superficial or partial

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the vocabulary to talk about how you keep informed: the press, television, radio and social media, with words like headline, coverage, broadcast or biased. It is essential for discussing the news in a conversation or in an oral exam. Spanish speakers find it hard because news is uncountable and takes a singular verb, there are false friends (editorial, notice, fountain) and the prepositions change: on TV, but in the newspaper.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of the media in English: the formats (newspaper, magazine, radio, podcast), the people (journalist, editor, presenter), the products (headline, article, report) and the digital world (post, share, go viral, fake news). It also includes adjectives to judge information, such as biased or unbiased.
contexto.por_que_importa: Discussing the news is one of the most common tasks in a conversation and in an oral exam, and it is a way into giving opinions on economics or politics. Mistakes like “a new”, “the news are” or “I read it on the newspaper” are very noticeable. False friends can cause misunderstandings: saying editorial for publisher makes people think of an opinion article.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used to say where you have read or seen something, to assess the reliability of a source or to talk about social media. The signals are verbs like read, watch, post or broadcast. Spanish speakers tend to make news plural, to use “on” with newspaper by analogy with on TV and to copy “fuente” as fountain.
